title: How Vaccines Train Your Immune System
summary: Vaccines work by training the immune system to recognize and attack specific antigens, though individual immune responses can vary due to factors like genetics.

scenes.text: How does your body learn to fight off dangerous diseases before they ever strike?
Antigen-presenting cells take up vaccine antigens, process them, and present them to T-cells to activate the adaptive immune system.
Tumor antigen vaccines work the same way as viral vaccines, training the immune system to target cells containing specific antigens.

items.title: Viral Vaccines
items.detail: Derived from viruses or infected cells.

scenes.text: Studies on dialysis patients show that individual factors like age, diabetes, and genetics can influence the immune response to vaccines.
The emerging field of vaccinomics studies how genetic polymorphism leads to individual and population variations in vaccine immune responses.
Vaccines successfully train the adaptive immune system by introducing specific antigens to trigger targeted defense mechanisms.

sources.title: Heterogeneity in vaccine immune response: the role of immunogenetics and the emerging field of vaccinomics
